title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, full execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, representative diagnostic artifacts, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness for such workflows requires generated configurations to satisfy deterministic invariants (reachability, policy compliance, workflow ordering, and group-level safety). Prior prototype systems and benchmarks illustrate feasibility but leave open questions about how much deterministic verification and bounded repair alter operational correctness when the same initial sample is reused across comparisons. This paper addresses that gap with a preregistered, artifact-grounded paired experiment.

Research question and estimand. Preregistered study CAND-2026-001 asked: under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does permitting at most one verifier-triggered automated repair improve the per-task rate at which a deterministic verifier accepts generated configurations? The primary estimand is the paired difference in per-task binary acceptance (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Because the experiment enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics the estimand isolates the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair on an identical initial candidate (a repair-only effect). This design does not measure effects due to independent guarded first-pass generations, constrained prompting, temperature tuning, or mult-sample selection.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, fully archived paired experiment executing 200 intent→configuration tasks with a deterministic verifier and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. (2) Complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation showing 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). (3) Artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis reporting baseline pass 199/200 and guarded pass 200/200 with contingency counts (n11=199,n10=1,n01=0,n00=0), paired risk difference 0.005, exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0, and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). (4) A focused failure diagnosis for the single repaired pair using archived validator traces. (5) Detailed reproducibility guidance and bounded limitations tied to archived artifacts and reconciliation records.
sections.related_work:
We conducted a fresh literature investigation and verified records covering intent→configuration systems, generate–validate–repair patterns, and agentic-AI safety discussions relevant to NetOps. Prior intent-to-configuration prototypes and task-bench evaluations demonstrate that LLMs can synthesize device configurations from operator intents and that in many settings verification is advocated as a necessary guardrail [1],[2],[3]. However, the supplied literature mainly reports prototype evaluations or cross-domain demonstrations; it does not provide widespread preregistered paired experiments that deterministically reuse identical initial samples to isolate repair-only effects. That observation motivated our paired shared_initial_candidate design.

Generate→validate→repair as a design pattern is documented in adjacent domains (program repair, synthesis with tests) and motivates guarded pipelines for operational tasks; these works indicate that bounded verifier-guided repair can improve correctness in software-engineering contexts, but they do not substitute for NetOps-specific verifier-backed empirical evidence [4],[5],[6]. Survey and safety literature on agentic AI and LLM deployment documents failure modes (hallucination/confabulation) and argues for verifier gates and provenance; that conceptual groundwork motivated our guarded design and strict oracle definition but does not provide the artifact-grounded NetOps verifier outcomes we report here [7],[8].

Synthesis and gap. The verified records show active work on intent-driven generators and proposals for guardrails, but they leave an empirical gap: few artifact-backed studies quantify the marginal verifier/repair effect when the exact same initial generated candidate is reused across conditions. Our experiment directly addresses that gap under tightly controlled deterministic verifier semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design freeze. We preregistered study CAND-2026-001 before execution. The preregistration defined the primary estimand, sampling plan (deterministic selection of 200 tasks from the deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5), generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (single sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused), and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. The preregistration also specified the confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar), primary handling of failures, sensitivity analyses treating persistent unparsables as failures, and a power rationale targeting detection of ≈10–15 percentage-point paired increases at N = 200 under mid-range baseline assumptions (~45–65%). The preregistration and execution plan are archived in the execution manifest and associated artifacts.

Task bank and task encoding. Tasks were generated deterministically (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) and targeted high-difficulty workflow patterns (very_hard and extreme). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (an ordered list of required discrete configuration actions), allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies (e.g., at-least-one-up constraints, final_group_constraints), difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count), and a normalized reference_answer. Representative archived tasks show required_command_count values ranging from 3 up to 9 and changed_interface_count up to 3 for extreme tasks; these manifest fields appear in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and in archived representative_task entries.

Model configuration and sampling semantics. The declared requested model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). That configuration records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly state that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0; the hosted model service may sample nondeterministically. The adapter enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Provider accounting in deterministic_reconciliation.json records stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1} and hosted_model_call_event_count = 201. The adapter's provider-call audit also shows cache_miss_count = 201 and cache_hit_count = 0, indicating fresh generation events for all shared initial calls.

Deterministic verifier and scoring rule. A deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) served as the oracle. The verifier parses candidate configurations, enforces per-device allowed-field constraints, tests required_sequence ordering constraints, evaluates group invariants (e.g., at-least-one-up, final_group_constraints), and checks dependency rules encoded in each task manifest. The binary scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation returns 1 iff all encoded invariants pass. Per-episode validator_trace artifacts include validation_before and validation_after states, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes, and a boolean valid flag. These traces are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ and provide the primary evidence supporting per-episode scoring decisions.

Paired execution semantics and failure handling. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics baseline and guarded episodes for each pair begin from the identical sampled candidate; any paired difference therefore arises solely from the permitted verifier-triggered repair. The missingness_plan specified deterministic attempts to sanitize minor formatting issues and a sensitivity analysis treating persistent unparsables as failures. In the archived run there were no persistent unparsables and no preregistered exclusions. All per-episode terminal_error_type fields are null in the scoring artifacts, consistent with successful scoring completion for every episode.

Statistical analysis and exact McNemar implementation. The primary confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar based on discordant pair counts n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) and n01 (guarded=0, baseline=1). Let n = n10 + n01 and k = n10. Under H0 (no directionality) k ~ Binomial(n, 0.5). The two-sided p is computed using the exact binomial tail rule: p = 2 * min{BinomCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 - BinomCDF(k - 1; n, 0.5)} with the conventional handling for k = 0. For our observed discordants (n = 1, k = 1) this yields p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile confidence intervals for the absolute risk difference were computed with 10,000 resamples and bootstrap_seed = 1729; the implementation and seed are archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and timing. The execution manifest records start and end timestamps (UTC) and provider-call accounting: the run started at 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00 and completed at 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00 (≈29 minutes total elapsed wall-clock time). Planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions) and completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call audit reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}, consistent with the adapter-enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and the single permitted repair call observed.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (archived CSV artifacts). analysis/condition_summary.csv shows:
- Baseline: successes = 199, failures = 1, observed = 200, success_rate = 0.995.
- Guarded: successes = 200, failures = 0, observed = 200, success_rate = 1.000.
The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) records n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Using the exact two-sided McNemar binomial calculation (n = 1, k = 1) yields p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.00, 0.015]; these values are identical to analysis/results.json and the archived CSVs.

Representative repaired case and failure diagnosis. The guarded pipeline invoked exactly one automated repair. Validator traces for the repaired pair reveal an extreme composite task with required_command_count = 9 and changed_interface_count = 3 where the shared initial candidate violated the task's required_sequence ordering constraint. The repair applied a minimal reordering aligning generated commands to the required_sequence; subsequent validation_after.valid = true. The per-episode validator_trace fields (validation_before.violation_codes, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration) document the violation and the post-repair correction. This localized diagnostic supports the preregistered hypothesis that multi-device ordering and cross-device dependency interactions concentrate failure risk in higher-difficulty tasks.

Missingness, exclusions, and contamination summary. The run recorded no preregistered exclusions and no persistent unparsables; analysis/missingness_summary.csv shows complete_pairs = 200 and zeros in all missingness categories. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty (no flagged contamination). Deterministic_reconciliation.json marks all deterministic consistency checks passed and pair_accounting_consistent = true. Provider-call audit shows cache_miss_count = 201 and cache_hit_count = 0, indicating fresh calls for every shared initial generation.

Exploratory diagnostics by difficulty and manifest metadata. Representative task manifests in the archived sample illustrate variation in difficulty metadata (required_command_count from 3 to 9; patterns labeled very_hard or extreme). The single failed baseline episode occurred on an extreme composite task among the highest required_command_count values in the sample, consistent with the preregistered exploratory expectation that multi-device sequencing and dependency complexity drive residual failure risk. analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg visualizes condition rates and the bootstrap distribution used for the CI calculation.

Compact numeric summaries. Table 1 (Primary confirmatory results) and Table 2 (Execution and task accounting) summarize the numeric outcomes and provider-stage counts. All numeric entries are drawn directly from archived CSV artifacts and the execution manifest; the analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv and analysis/results.json) provide the authoritative records.
sections.discussion:
Estimand interpretation and design implications. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the observed paired difference isolates the marginal effect of permitting at most one verifier-triggered repair on an identical sampled candidate. This design intentionally excludes other guarded interventions (independent guarded generations, constrained prompts, multi-sample selection). Consequently, the present experiment measures a repair-only effect and readers should not generalize these results to alternative pipeline variants without new experiments.

Statistical regime, power, and interpretation. Our preregistered power rationale targeted detection of moderate absolute paired increases (~10–15 percentage points) at N = 200 under baseline assumptions near 45–65%. The actual baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) greatly exceeded those assumptions, placing the analysis into a discrete discordant-count regime where the exact McNemar p-value is uninformative (p = 1.0 for the observed discordants). The paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] provides a practical bound on plausible effect sizes compatible with the data; it shows the data are consistent with at most small absolute improvements under our design. This outcome emphasizes that unexpectedly high baseline performance reduces realized inferential sensitivity for small repair-only effects.

Operational implications and bounded claims. The single repaired failure was a multi-device ordering breach detectable by the deterministic verifier and correctable by the bounded repair routine. Artifact-grounded evidence therefore supports a narrow operational conclusion: in this synthetic deterministic task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a verifier-triggered bounded repair corrected a localized ordering fault on an identical initial candidate. This does not imply that guarded repair will systematically correct semantic intent misunderstandings, omissions only observable in dataplane execution, or errors induced by adversarially poisoned contexts. Broader operational claims require multi-model studies, independent-first-pass guarded semantics, live emulation or dataplane tests, and adversarial contamination experiments.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: paired shared_initial_candidate semantics ensure the estimand focuses on repair effects and avoid confounding from independent sampling, but they do not address prompt sensitivity or sampling variance. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces manifested invariants encoded in task manifests but cannot substitute for live dataplane execution—some runtime behaviors and device-specific interactions remain unmodeled. External validity: the experiment used one model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank; generalization to other models, prompt templates, vendor firmware, or production heterogeneity is not established. Conclusion validity: with only one discordant pair observed the sampling uncertainty for small absolute effects is substantial; the bootstrap CI quantifies this uncertainty.

Reproducibility and reanalysis guidance. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle. Key artifacts enabling reanalysis include: the execution manifest and execution/task_manifest.jsonl (task selection and manifests), execution/model_configuration.json (declared model and sampling fields), execution/responses/ (shared-initial and per-condition responses), execution/scoring/ (validator_trace per episode), analysis/*.csv (paired contingency and condition summaries), deterministic_reconciliation.json (provider accounting and stage_counts), and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (bootstrap parameters and seed). Reanalysis using the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor will reproduce the confirmatory numbers reported above. The initial master prompt is archived and immutable (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA-256 included in the Disclosure Statement). For sensitivity, the preregistration-specified alternative treatment of persistent unparsables as failures is supported by the archived artifacts but was not needed because no persistent unparsables occurred.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In 200 synthetic deterministic tasks with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. The paired absolute risk difference was 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the single discordant pair under the exact binomial formulation described in Methods. Artifact-grounded evidence supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting, but broader operational claims require larger, multi-model, adversarial, and live-device studies. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts supporting these results are archived and indexed by the execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). The deterministic verifier used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and indexed by the execution manifest.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
